# jenkins_credential_domain (Resource)

Manages a credentials domain within a Jenkins credentials store. Domains group credentials so that resources can place them into a named store via their `domain` argument.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "jenkins_credential_domain" "example" {
  name        = "github"
  description = "Credentials for github.com"
}

# Place a credential into the domain via its `domain` argument:
resource "jenkins_credential_username" "example" {
  name                = "github-bot"
  domain              = jenkins_credential_domain.example.name
  username            = "bot"
  password_wo         = var.bot_token
  password_wo_version = "1"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the domain. Changing this forces a new domain to be created.

### Optional

- `description` (String) A human readable description of the domain.
- `folder` (String) The folder whose credentials store holds the domain. If not set, the global store is used. Changing this forces a new domain to be created.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The canonical identifier of the domain, `[<folder>/]<name>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Credential domains can be imported using their canonical ID: [<folder>/]<name>
terraform import jenkins_credential_domain.example /github
```
